description:
Combinamos vocación aeroespacial, ingeniería y narrativa para rescatar el legado de las misiones pioneras de la NASA en la Luna y Marte. Como centinelas de la memoria espacial, revivimos la guardia eterna de los exploradores mecánicos que abrieron camino en el cosmos. Buscamos compañeros con interés en desarrollo web, modelado 3D, diseño visual o redacción técnica para estructurar una experiencia digital inmersiva.

¡Únete y forma parte de la tripulación!
summary:
RELICS 10.0 is an interactive educational platform developed by Team 04, Centinelas del Vacío, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms the history of abandoned and retired space exploration equipment into engaging learning experiences.

The platform features nine mission-based simulations, 675 scientific questions across three difficulty levels, educational documentary videos, and an interactive 3D assembly laboratory.

The project uses historical NASA ALSEP/EASEP data and official NASA mission resources to connect scientific information with interactive exploration. Its goal is to help students understand the scientific legacy of space missions and discover how equipment can continue teaching us long after its original mission ends.
details:
RELICS 10.0: Explorers of the Forgotten is a browser-based educational platform inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten."

Problem

Space exploration missions leave behind vehicles, instruments, and scientific equipment that have contributed significantly to our understanding of the Moon, Mars, and the Solar System. However, their historical importance and scientific achievements can be difficult for younger learners to understand through traditional technical documentation.

Our solution

RELICS 10.0 transforms these historical missions into interactive educational experiences that combine scientific storytelling, simulation, visualization, and assessment.

Nine interactive missions

  1. Eagle – Apollo 11 lunar landing module.
  2. LRV-3 – Apollo 17 lunar rover.
  3. ALSEP – Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package.
  4. Sojourner – Mars Pathfinder rover.
  5. Opportunity – Mars exploration rover.
  6. InSight – Martian seismic investigation.
  7. Ingenuity – Mars helicopter.
  8. Dawn – Exploration of Ceres.
  9. Pioneer 10 – Deep-space communication and exploration.

Each mission introduces a scientific challenge inspired by historical NASA equipment.

Educational question bank

The platform contains 675 questions organized into nine missions, three difficulty levels, and 25 questions per mission at each level. The questions include answer explanations and scientific references.

Interactive 3D laboratory

Students can explore four educational 3D reconstructions, including a rover and the Apollo 11 lunar module. They can manipulate the models, inspect individual components, and explore assembly relationships.

Scientific data integration

The project incorporates historical NASA ALSEP/EASEP data, including lunar experiment station information, planned operating lifetimes, and communication frequencies. These data were curated and processed using Python to support the educational interface.

Other official NASA mission resources provide historical and scientific context for the remaining missions.

Multimedia resources

Nine educational documentary videos are embedded through the YouTube player and credited to their respective creators.

Technologies

The platform uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, and browser-based 3D visualization technologies. The source code is publicly available on GitHub under the MIT license, with external resources credited separately.

Limitations

The simulations use simplified educational models and illustrative parameters. They do not reproduce actual NASA spacecraft telemetry. Individual scores are stored in the browser, while online multiplayer requires a separately hosted WebSocket server.

Expected impact

RELICS aims to make space exploration history more accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, and provide teachers with an interactive resource for introducing engineering and planetary science concepts.

Future work includes classroom evaluation, accessibility improvements, and further validation of the educational experience.
